newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HAUGE ALLOWED TO ACT AS SOLSKJAER'S MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HAUGE ALLOWED TO ACT AS SOLSKJAER'S MANAGER.

text.p: Norwegian Rune Hauge, banned by FIFA from working as an agent, has been cleared to act as personal manager to compatriot Ole Gunnar Solskjaer of Manchester United.
Hauge has been refused a licence to become an official FIFA agent and is currently facing fraud charges in Norway and a possible jail sentence.
Hauge was involved in the payoff deal that cost George Graham his job as manager of Arsenal last year.
The English Football Association said on Friday that although Hauge could act as Solskjaer's manager, he could play no part in any transfer or contract negotiations.
F.A. spokesman Steve Double said: "There is no ruling against Hauge helping Solskjaer with commercial activities, but he must not get involved with club contracts or any transfer business."

Solskjaer, who has scored five goals for Manchester United in only eight games since his 1.5 million pounds ($2.36 million) move from Molde, believes Hauge is the ideal man to promote his commercial interests and United have raised no public objection.
United's assistant secretary, Ken Ramsden, said on Friday: "There is no problem for us because there is no ban on Rune Hauge being involved in this kind of commercial activity in this country."

However, United are thought to be embarrassed about the 23-year-old Solskjaer's link with an unlicensed agent who is also under investigation over the transfer of Norwegian defender Alf Inge Haaland to Nottingham Forest two years ago.
Solskjaer's first commercial deal looks likely to be a boot sponsorship worth 100,000 pounds ($157,500) a year.
